findings.title: The set-arm capture `extra` has no closed key set, so a prose or unbounded per-row field can be added to a Sentry error report with the whole eval still green
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The single-row arm pins its payload twice — `Object.keys(extra).sort()` against SINGLE_ROW_EXTRA_KEYS at write.test.ts:1531 and an exhaustive `toEqual` at :1532 — and RT-M9 proved that pin real by killing a `refusal_code` leak. The set arm has neither. Its only case asserts `extra.row_count === 3`, `extra.refusal_lanes === 'ask_withheld'`, and a `not.toContain(subjectId)` loop; the `not.toContain` proxy catches only values that happen to be the fixture's UUIDs. Adding `refusal_codes: inputs.map(r => r.refusalCode).join(',')` survived that case (RT-M14) and survived the full four-suite sweep including both live-DB suites (RT-M16, 146/146 green). The mutation is executed by the case, is observably different, and violates a named intake invariant ('Sentry extra and tags carry only closed enums and UUIDs. No review text, no response text, no refusal_code prose, no unbounded per-row id lists') and the writer's own docblock at write.ts:743-747. It is neither equivalent nor unexecuted. Concrete scenario: an `ask_withheld` build withholds 5,000 Asks and the set INSERT violates a 116 CHECK; a later maintainer, reasoning from the same 'more context helps triage' impulse the diff itself resisted, adds the codes to `extra`; 5,000 free-ish gate-reason strings ride an error envelope into Sentry, past the redaction discipline CLAUDE.md and ADR 0023 impose, and no test turns red. The fix is one line: pin the set-arm key set the way SINGLE_ROW_EXTRA_KEYS pins the single-row one.

findings.title: `extra.refusal_lanes` is asserted only against a single-lane fixture, so it can silently degrade to the first input's lane
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Two cases touch the set arm. The multi-lane one ('attributes a set-arm write failure with the distinct sources sorted and comma-joined', write.test.ts:1560) deliberately uses an unsorted, duplicated, two-lane fixture and asserts `tags` and `level` — it never reads `extra`. The extra case ('carries row_count and never per-row subject ids in the set-arm capture extra', write.test.ts:1596) uses a three-row SINGLE-lane fixture, where the distinct-sorted string and `inputs[0].refusalSource` are the same value. Replacing `refusal_lanes: lanes` with `refusal_lanes: inputs[0]!.refusalSource` survived (RT-M15) and survived the four-suite sweep (RT-M16). The mutation is executed and observably different for any mixed cohort. It is not equivalent: `WriteRefusalEventInput[]` permits a mixed array, which is the exact edge case the intake enumerates, and the key exists precisely to be the durable full-set copy. Concrete scenario: a future lane batches two sources; the set INSERT fails; the Sentry event names one lane in `extra` while the tag names two, and an operator triaging a mixed-cohort ledger fault reads a payload that contradicts its own tag. Fix: assert `extra.refusal_lanes` on the MULTI-lane case, not the single-lane one.
